sections.title: Reading
sections.instructions: Read the text about ants, then complete Activities 1–6 below.
sections.passage:
Have you ever spent any time watching what goes on around an anthill? If not, you really should. Even though ants are tiny insects, they are truly amazing creatures.

Ants are kind of like humans, because they live in big "ant cities" that are called "colonies." In the colonies, thousands of ants work together to build a shelter, find food and protect their young. Ants live in a system of underground tunnels that they work hard to dig out. In these tunnels, there are special rooms for storing food and nurseries for baby ants. Some ants are in charge of keeping the colony clean. These ants have to pick up all the garbage from the colony and bring it to a garbage pile outside the colony. Do you think all that lifting might be too much for a little ant? Think again. Even though they are so small, ants can lift up to 20 times their own weight. That's about as much as a 10 year-old boy lifting a small car.

The entrance to their underground world is what we call an "anthill." The anthill is a small pile of sand and dirt that thousands of ants work together to build. In the middle is a little hole through which the ants can climb down into their underground city. Imagine trying to organize such a task! You'd think that ants must be very good communicators.

The tricky part about ants is that they can't talk. But this doesn't stop these little creatures. Ants communicate by releasing different chemicals from their bodies for other ants to smell. For instance, if an ant finds a piece of food, it will send out a chemical signal that says "there is food here." The other ants will follow their noses toward the pile of food until it is all gone. On the other hand, if there is something dangerous around, ants will send a chemical signal that says "stay away." Each colony of ants has its own special smell. This way ants can tell if there are intruders among them.

The most important job for ants is to protect the Queen. Each ant colony has a Queen, the ant who lays the eggs. Queen ants can live up to fifteen years!

Besides bothering us on picnics, ants pose a few other problems for humans. Some ants like to build their nests in wood, which can then cause our homes or porches to rot. But on the other hand, ants help to keep our soil healthy because the holes that they dig allow air and water to get down into the earth. So next time you see a trail of ants or the top of an anthill, stop and think about how amazing these little creatures are and what their lives must be like.

Activity 1 — Read the sentence and choose TRUE or FALSE (example: "Ants have nurseries for baby ants." — TRUE):

Activity 1 — Read the sentence and choose TRUE or FALSE:

Activity 1 — Read the sentence and choose TRUE or FALSE:

Activity 1 — Read the sentence and choose TRUE or FALSE:

Activity 1 — Read the sentence and choose TRUE or FALSE:

Each ant colony has fifteen queens.

Activity 2 — Read the story and answer.

**Which three behaviors of ants show that they are hard-working?** Write the letters of the three correct options, separated by commas (e.g. a, b, d).

a) They work together to build shelter, find food and protect their young
b) Thousands of ants work to build the anthill and tunnels
c) The ants clean out the garbage from their colony
d) The ants communicate with smells

Activity 2 — Read the story and choose the correct answer.

**What would probably happen if the Queen ant suddenly died?**

choices.text: There would be no more eggs
There would be no more new ants

questions.prompt:

Activity 5 — Complete the sentence with the base or root word of the word in brackets. (Example: Ants **communicate** by releasing or sending out smells to other ants. (communicators))

Activity 6 — Look at the word in bold and decide whether it is used as a NOUN or a VERB. (Example: The ants **work** together to build tunnels. — VERB; The **work** of the ants is hard. — NOUN)

Answer the following questions in at least 7 sentences. Feel free to write more if you can.

1. **If you have a chance to meet an ant, what questions will you ask it?**
2. **Give some suggestions to ants on how they can live better.**
3. **Have you ever seen ants in life? Share your experience with ants.**
4. **Use 3 adjectives to describe ants.**
questions.criteria:
Content (up to 4 pts): the response addresses all four questions — questions to ask an ant, suggestions for ants, personal experience with ants, and exactly 3 adjectives describing ants.
Length (1 pt): at least 7 complete sentences.
Grammar and spelling (up to 3 pts): mostly correct sentence structure, verb forms, and spelling; minor errors do not block meaning.
Vocabulary and coherence (up to 2 pts): appropriate word choice for Grade 5 and logically connected ideas.
